intent.raw: Lean-native finite-model search (single trust base) vs Cedar/Datalog (SMT, Lean-verified core) vs Alloy/Z3 (separate trust base)
intent.objective: Refine the open Row-2 decision from the accepted FOL constitution-validation dispatch: which engine runs the bounded cross-rule / whole-constitution satisfiability search, weighing single-trust-base (Lean) against best-fit expressiveness/maturity (Datalog/Alloy), adjudicated by the transitive-closure toy-game witness; output a non-executed plan for the section-5a first step.
intent.operator_sentence: refine the Row-2 solver trust-base decision

route_menu.context_hint: Three named engines compete on one criteria set; the decisive discriminator is transitive-closure expressiveness, tested by the Goedel-witness toy game.

items.label: Lean-native finite-model search
items.description: Do the bounded finite-model / decide search in Lean; one trust base, reuse the kernel; hand-build reach/acyclicity.

items.label: Cedar + Datalog (FORGE/PCAS)
items.description: External relational solver whose Cedar core is itself Lean-verified; Datalog supplies recursion/reachability.

items.label: Alloy/Kodkod or Z3
items.description: Mature bounded model-finder with native transitive closure; separate SAT/SMT trust base.

technique_overlays.trigger: The decision needs the canonical ten-stage Refine loop before any next-route execution.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every non-first step consumes prior evidence; every pass verdict is backed by an artifact or an explicit blocked reason.

technique_overlays.trigger: Three named engines compete and the trust-base tradeoff must be made explicit, not assumed.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The selected engine records why it beats the other two on the criteria set and the toy-game result.

technique_overlays.trigger: Competing principles: single-trust-base minimization vs best-fit expressiveness/maturity.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: A tensioned pair argues each pole with a named anti-bias axis and predicted disagreement; rejected reasoning is kept in a residue ledger.

technique_overlays.trigger: Three plausible engines must be scored and dominated options dropped.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Engines are scored on trust-base, transitive-closure expressiveness, decidability/soundness, build cost, maintenance, and whole-ruleset performance; a Pareto gate drops dominated options and the winner recomposes the Row-2 obligation.

technique_overlays.trigger: A selected engine must be shown to express and block the Goedel-witness cycle the per-rule validator passes, before planning.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The capability matrix records, per engine, whether it can EXPRESS and DECIDE governs-acyclicity on the 3-node cyclic fixture; engines that cannot are eliminated with a cited failure reason.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The engine choice has a real confirmation-bias risk (the findings already lean Lean-native) and a research-heavy expressiveness question; tensioned lanes cancel the bias and isolate the legwork.
subagent_strategy.explanation: A tensioned dialectic pair argues the two poles (single-trust-base vs best-fit-tool) and a neutral toy-game falsifier renders the transitive-closure capability matrix; parent synthesizes. Operator confirmed this tensioned shape at the strategy gate.
context: Decision sits on the accepted 2026-06-28 FOL dispatch (Row-2 bounded; weigh Lean-native first).
Discriminator is transitive-closure expressiveness, an empirical capability question.

roles.purpose: Argue Option A and honestly assess Lean bounded finite-model-search ergonomics for reach/acyclicity.
Argue Options B/C; pick Datalog vs Alloy on native recursion/transitive-closure; concede the second-trust-base cost.
Neutral capability matrix for Lean, Cedar, Datalog, Alloy/Z3 on the Goedel-witness acyclicity fixture.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Operator confirmed the standard refine route with the recommended tensioned subagents at the strategy gate.
receipt_requirements: Each subagent writes a stage receipt memo under stages/; parent verifies on disk (P8) before design synthesis; anti-bias axis (foundation-minimization vs capability-maximization) and predicted disagreement recorded.

steps.name: Context Builder evidence baseline
stop_conditions: The three options and their trust bases have concrete cites.
The Row-2 obligation and the Goedel-witness fixture are named with source paths.

steps.name: Invoke Define for the engine decision
Invoke Design — dialectic + tournament over the three engines
convergence_criteria: Both poles scored against trust-base, transitive-closure expressiveness, decidability, build cost, maintenance, whole-ruleset performance.
Pareto gate drops dominated engines; a single owning verdict (or explicit staged combination) is named.

steps.name: Distill Repair — toy-game falsification of the engine choice
Invoke Plan — non-executed build plan for the section-5a first step

gates.condition: Runtime-backed stages and subagent spawning waited for explicit operator confirmation after the strategy preview.
REFINE-DISPATCH.json validates with the repo-local dispatch-spec validator before stage execution.
The dialectic pair carries a named anti-bias axis (foundation-minimization vs capability-maximization) and a predicted disagreement before spawn.
The engine verdict is backed by the toy-game capability matrix; an engine that cannot express governs-acyclicity cannot be selected as the acyclicity engine.
The recommendation does not exceed what the toy-game evidence and the accepted FOL findings sustain; build-from-owned framing preserved (no KILL of an owned engine).
Refine produces a non-executed plan only; building the solver is a separate Task Session next-route.

boundaries.contract: The accepted FOL findings are read-only authority inputs; this run resolves only the open Row-2 engine decision.
Refine writes only into its run folder and emits a non-executed plan; building the solver is a separate Task Session.

state_namespaces.write_policy: read-only authority input in this run

promotion_guardrails: Do not mark any of the three engines KILL; the accepted FOL findings make all three build-from-owned candidates.
Do not select an engine as the acyclicity engine without toy-game evidence it can express transitive closure.
Do not build the solver inside this refine run; emit a non-executed plan and a Task Session next-route only.
Do not let the recommendation exceed what the toy-game evidence and the accepted findings sustain.
